property_summary: c.Collect must revert if MinSum is always zero unless the sender's balance meets a non-zero MinSum.
c.Collect(amt) must revert when called after c.Put(amt) with MinSum=1 and initialized.
c.Collect(amt) must revert when called after c.Put{value: amt}(lockTime) with MinSum=1 and initialized.
c.Collect(amt) must revert when called after c.Put{value: amt}(lockTime) with MinSum=1 and initialized.
c.Collect(amt) must revert when called after c.Put{value: amt}(lockTime) with MinSum=1 and initialized.

For any input, after initialization and a Collect call, the reference contract's MinSum equals the last value set via SetMinSum, while the mutant's MinSum is always zero, violating the invariant that MinSum is only settable before initialization.

After Initialize followed by SetMinSum with any positive amount, Collect cannot succeed for amounts smaller than that MinSum in the reference, but the mutant allows Collect for any amount because MinSum is forced to zero.

After initialization and any sequence of Put calls, a Collect that succeeds must leave MinSum unchanged from its initial value in the reference, but the mutant breaks this by allowing MinSum to be overwritten later.

After initialization, MinSum must equal whatever was last set via SetMinSum before initialization; the mutant lets SetMinSum reset MinSum to zero even after initialization, breaking the invariant that post-initialization calls to SetMinSum revert.

After initialization, MinSum can only be non-zero if it was set before initialization; the mutant always has MinSum zero, so when initialized and a non-zero MinSum was set beforehand, collecting with any amount less than that MinSum succeeds in the mutant but fails in the reference.
MinSum can be set to a non-zero value after initialization
After any call to SetMinSum, the returned value of MinSum() must equal the argument passed; the bug forces MinSum to 0 regardless of the argument.
For any call to SetMinSum, if the contract has not been initialized, the value of MinSum matches the argument after the call; the bug sets it to 0 regardless of the argument.
After any non-reverting call to SetMinSum when the contract is uninitialized, the stored MinSum must equal the supplied _val; the bug always sets MinSum to 0 instead of _val.
After a successful call to SetMinSum while uninitialized, MinSum is exactly the argument; the mutant wrongly sets MinSum to 0 regardless.

For any admissible call to SetMinSum, if the contract is uninitialized, the resulting MinSum must equal the argument _val; the bug sets MinSum to 0 regardless, which can be distinguished by observing that after a subsequent successful Collect (or other behavior), the MinSum threshold affects withdrawal ability.
MinSum can be set successfully to a positive value before initialization.
SetMinSum reverts on the uninitialized contract only when the contract has already been initialized.
Setting LogFile always reverts, so no LogFile.AddMessage can ever succeed
SetLogFile does not revert if the contract has not been initialized

property_summary: LogFile can be set to a non-zero address even when intitalized is false.
Calling SetLogFile successfully sets the log file address when it is the first call to the contract, but the mutant prevents any address from being set.
SetLogFile only reverts if the contract was already initialized
After c.Initialized() is called, c.SetLogFile(anyAddr) must not change the LogFile; the buggy version allows changing it thereafter.
Once the contract is initialized, the LogFile address must remain immutable; the buggy SetLogFile allows overwriting it after initialization, violating the intended immutability invariant.
After initialization, the LogFile address must remain unchanged; the buggy SetLogFile lets it be overwritten post‑init.
After initialization, any call to SetLogFile must fail or leave the LogFile address unchanged; the buggy version allows the LogFile address to be overwritten after initialization.
After any call to Put, the caller's recorded balance in Acc[caller].balance must equal the total Ether sent by them through Put, but the mutant fails to increment it and thus violates this invariant.

After a successful Put, the sum of all Acc balances must be strictly positive when the contract holds Ether, but the mutant fails to increment the sender's balance, making the sum zero while Ether is held.
